ticket.description:
# KS-1054 N-1350-7b DEPLOY-ALL-RC1-WORDING — deploy-all.sh's rc-1 smoke value says "failed or could not be verified", because rc 1 is also a missing parser

File: `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh`
Test file: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh`  (NEW file)
Tip: `3e3a68260d0ef541b2410d323849d2639ddd6941` (origin develop, `git ls-remote` 2026-09-30 13:20 AEST)
Runner: `bash` (bash 3.2, `bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh` from the repo root)

Written 2026-09-30 13:20 AEST from `3e3a68260d0e`, product call site `:295`-`:314` and helpers `:271`-`:289`, and the whole reference suite read. Brief-writer sub-agent for Wednesday. Source: gate47 QA report (`Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-30-batch1349-g47/report.md`, sha256 `e0eb8ba1eb26…`), finding N-1350-7 at `:374` (Polish). gate47 named deploy.sh only; THIS is the same false claim in deploy-all.sh, found by the brief-writer reading the twin call site (the "b" in the slug). The deploy.sh half is a separate brief (`KS-1054-N-1350-7`).

## The mode — read this twice

CODE+TEST. Your diff touches EXACTLY 2 files, in this order:
1. `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh` — modified in place: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh`, EXACTLY the ONE hunk under "The exact change", byte for byte.
2. `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh` — a NEW file: `--- /dev/null` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh`, EXACTLY the hunk under "The test", byte for byte.

You never touch any other file. The `reference_test_file` in your input (`ks1054_deploy_scripts_read_startup_migrations.test.sh`) is shape reference only — do NOT touch it, do NOT add cells to it. You do NOT touch `check-startup-migrations.sh` or `deploy.sh`.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`deploy-all.sh` calls the shared predicate at `:303` and routes its rc through a `case` at `:304`-`:314`. The `*)` arm (`:311`-`:313`) calls `smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "one or more failed"` (`:312`); `smoke_test` (`:278`-`:289`) prints `✗ $name (expected $expected, got $actual)` and counts a FAIL. But the predicate exits 1 for more than a failed count: it also exits 1 when python3 is missing (`check-startup-migrations.sh:77`-`:81`) and when `failed` is not an integer (the ks1054 suite's P6, `:68`-`:69`). So with python3 missing the smoke line reads "got one or more failed" — a claim that migrations were read and failed, when they were never read. gate47 measured exactly this in deploy.sh (report `:167`, N-1350-7); the twin line here has the same shape. The FAIL count and the deploy's exit are RIGHT and stay; only the reported VALUE changes, to name both causes.

## Where

- `:312` — **the rc-1 smoke value: must say "failed or could not be verified"** (must change)
- `:313` — `    ;;` (correct) stays

## The exact change

ONE hunk. It replaces `:312` with three lines: two comment lines, then the new `smoke_test` line. Context: `:309`-`:311` before, `:313`-`:314` after (the blank `:315` is NOT context). Old side 6, new side 8. No context line is blank. The new `smoke_test` line contains a non-ASCII em dash `—` (U+2014), as does context line `:309`; copy both exactly.

```
--- a/Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh
+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh
@@ -309,6 +309,8 @@
     smoke_skip "Startup migrations" "the check did not run — see above"
     ;;
   *)
-    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "one or more failed"
+    # rc 1 is a failed count OR a count that could not be read (python3 missing, a non-integer
+    # `failed`), so the reported value must not claim the migrations were read (gate47 N-1350-7).
+    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "failed or could not be verified — see above"
     ;;
 esac
```

Both comment lines are byte-exact — the second one starts with a backtick-quoted `failed`; copy the backticks. The new `smoke_test` line keeps `"Startup migrations"` and `"0 failed"` exactly, and only its THIRD argument changes, to `"failed or could not be verified — see above"`.

**Do NOT touch** anything else in deploy-all.sh: not the `0)` arm `:305`-`:307`, not the `2)` arm `:308`-`:310` (its SKIP wording stays), not the call at `:303`, not the comment block `:295`-`:301` (its first line is the marker the tests extract by), not `esac` at `:314` (the tests' extraction ends on it — it must stay at column 0), not `smoke_test`/`smoke_skip` `:271`-`:289`.

## The test

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh` (NEW)

The shape to copy is the reference suite's deploy-all.sh call-site driver at `:351`-`:379` (`ALL_MARKER`, the `awk` extraction ending on `^esac$`, `drive_all_callsite` writing a stub `check-startup-migrations.sh` that exits a chosen rc, `smoke_test`/`smoke_skip`/`curl` stubbed). The new file's `smoke_test` stub ALSO prints `GOT <value>` for a failed comparison, so a cell can read the reported value, and it does not pipe to `tail -1`. There is no network, no Azure, no real predicate — only deploy-all.sh's own call-site bytes against a stub.

Emit this text as the new-file hunk, every line prefixed `+`, nothing added or dropped:

```
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# TESTS for gate47 N-1350-7 (deploy-all.sh twin) — the rc-1 smoke value must not claim the migrations were read
+# =============================================================================
+# check-startup-migrations.sh exits 1 for a FAILED count and ALSO for a count it could not read
+# (python3 missing, or `failed` not an integer). deploy-all.sh's `*)` arm reported the value
+# "one or more failed" for every one of them, which is false when the parser was missing.
+# deploy-all.sh's own call-site bytes are extracted by marker and EXECUTED against a STUB predicate
+# that exits with a chosen rc (the shape of the ks1054 suite's R8 cells).
+#
+# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_all_rc1_message.test.sh
+# =============================================================================
+set -uo pipefail
+#
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ALL="$HERE/../../deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh"
+#
+pass=0; fail=0
+ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
+bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n       %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }
+#
+[[ -f "$ALL" ]] || { echo "FATAL: subject not found at $ALL" >&2; exit 2; }
+#
+ALL_MARKER='# 1b. KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — startup migrations.'
+ALL_HITS=$(grep -cF "$ALL_MARKER" "$ALL" || true)
+if [[ "$ALL_HITS" == "1" ]]; then
+  ok "N0 deploy-all.sh's migration call site is locatable by marker (1 occurrence)"
+else
+  bad "N0 deploy-all.sh's migration call site is locatable by marker" "expected 1 occurrence, found $ALL_HITS"
+fi
+ALL_BLOCK=$(awk -v m="$ALL_MARKER" 'index($0,m){f=1} f{print} f&&/^esac$/{exit}' "$ALL")
+#
+drive_all_callsite() { # $1 = stub predicate rc -> "GOT <value>" for a failed smoke test, then "PASS=<n> FAIL=<n> SKIP=<n>"
+  local stubrc="$1" dir
+  dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/n1350_7_allsite.XXXXXX")"
+  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit %s\n' "$stubrc" > "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
+  chmod +x "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
+  {
+    printf 'PASS=0; FAIL=0; SKIP=0\n'
+    printf 'smoke_test() { if [ "$3" = "$2" ]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf "GOT %%s\\n" "$3"; fi; }\n'
+    printf 'smoke_skip() { SKIP=$((SKIP+1)); printf "SKIPPED %%s\\n" "$2"; }\n'
+    printf 'API=http://127.0.0.1:1\nHEALTH_BODY=\x27{"status":"healthy"}\x27\n'
+    printf 'curl() { printf %%s "$HEALTH_BODY"; }\n'
+    printf '%s\n' "$ALL_BLOCK"
+    printf 'printf "PASS=%%s FAIL=%%s SKIP=%%s\\n" "$PASS" "$FAIL" "$SKIP"\n'
+  } > "$dir/drive.sh"
+  ( cd "$dir" && bash ./drive.sh 2>/dev/null < /dev/null )
+  rm -rf "$dir"
+}
+#
+if [[ -z "$ALL_BLOCK" ]]; then
+  bad "N1 rc 1 names both causes" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
+  bad "N2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts a FAIL" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
+  bad "N3 CONTROL rc 2 is still a SKIP" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
+else
+  OUT_FAIL=$(drive_all_callsite 1)
+  if [[ "$OUT_FAIL" == *"GOT failed or could not be verified"* ]]; then
+    ok "N1 rc 1 reports failed OR could not be verified, so a missing parser is not reported as read migrations"
+  else
+    bad "N1 rc 1 names both causes" "printed: $OUT_FAIL"
+  fi
+  if [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT_FAIL" | tail -1)" == "PASS=0 FAIL=1 SKIP=0" ]]; then
+    ok "N2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts a FAIL, so the wording change did not weaken the check"
+  else
+    bad "N2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts a FAIL" "printed: $OUT_FAIL"
+  fi
+  OUT_SKIP=$(drive_all_callsite 2)
+  if [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT_SKIP" | tail -1)" == "PASS=0 FAIL=0 SKIP=1" && "$OUT_SKIP" != *"GOT "* ]]; then
+    ok "N3 CONTROL rc 2 is still a SKIP and reports no failed value"
+  else
+    bad "N3 CONTROL rc 2 is still a SKIP" "printed: $OUT_SKIP"
+  fi
+fi
+#
+echo
+echo "n1350-7 deploy-all.sh rc-1 message: $pass passed, $fail failed"
+[[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
```

Every `+` line is byte-exact — copy them. Several `printf` lines carry `\n`, `\\n`, `%%s`, `$((PASS+1))` and `\x27` inside single quotes — keep every backslash, percent sign and dollar sign exactly. Several lines (the header comments and `ALL_MARKER`) contain the em dash `—` — copy it. No `+` line is blank (the spacer lines are a single `#`).

## Red cells

- N1 rc 1 reports failed OR could not be verified

## Cells and controls

- `N1` = `N1 rc 1 reports failed OR could not be verified, so a missing parser is not reported as read migrations`   ← RED at the tip (measured: `FAIL N1 rc 1 names both causes` / `printed: GOT one or more failed`), GREEN with the fix
- `N0` = `N0 deploy-all.sh's migration call site is locatable by marker (1 occurrence)`   ← FIXTURE, GREEN throughout
- `N2` = `N2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts a FAIL, so the wording change did not weaken the check`   ← CONTROL, GREEN throughout
- `N3` = `N3 CONTROL rc 2 is still a SKIP and reports no failed value`   ← CONTROL, GREEN throughout

Whole new file: tip 3 passed / 1 failed (rc 1); with the product hunk 4 passed / 0 failed (rc 0). Measured, see Premises.

## The failing case (the "tamper")

The tamper IS the untouched tip: revert the product hunk and N1 goes red by ASSERTION (the reported value is `one or more failed`), not by a load error; N0/N2/N3 stay green. The tip line `    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "one or more failed"` occurs exactly ONCE in deploy-all.sh (literal count, Premises).

## Premises (each one measured, with where)

- `:312` is `    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "one or more failed"` (4 leading spaces), `:313` `    ;;`, `:314` `esac`, `:315` blank — read at the tip with `cat -et`.
- `smoke_test` `:278`-`:289` prints `  ✗ $name (expected $expected, got $actual)` and increments FAIL when `$actual != $expected` — read at the tip.
- The marker `# 1b. KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — startup migrations.` is `:295`, 1 occurrence — read at the tip.
- The predicate exits 1 when python3 is absent (`check-startup-migrations.sh:77`-`:81`) and for a non-integer `failed` (reference suite P6 `:68`-`:69`).
- New test at the tip (scratch clone at `3e3a68260d0e`, macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57): rc 1, "3 passed, 1 failed", the one FAIL is N1 by assertion; 0 load-error lines.
- New test with the product hunk (the golden): rc 0, "4 passed, 0 failed"; `bash -n` rc 0 on both files.
- Sibling: the reference suite names `deploy-all.sh` (so the checker's B6 runs it); on the golden it reads "36 passed, 0 failed" — its R8/R8b/R8c read counters, and `smoke_test`'s third argument only feeds its FAIL branch.
- Collision: 23 open PRs (REST `GET /pulls?state=open`); 0 of them list `deployment/azure/deploy-all.sh`, `deploy.sh`, `check-startup-migrations.sh` or this test path in `/files`. Positive control: the same matcher counts 2 `aktoRateLimit` paths in #1351.
- Golden: `golden.diff` beside this brief, sha256 `146819a1616e3a2ec4e0f6eae92bf776b4a7a191f1397a662fee55270bd3c377`, 2 files, 80 `+` / 1 `-`.

## UNMEASURED — stated rather than glossed

- `deploy-all.sh dev --skip-build` was NOT driven end to end (no Azure). The value is measured only through the extracted call site against stub helpers.
- The wording is the brief-writer's choice and deliberately matches the deploy.sh brief (`FAILED or could not be verified — see above`). gate47 did not name this line; the raising seat may reword or drop it.
- GNU bash / ubuntu (CI's `run-shell-suites.sh`) NOT run; macOS bash 3.2.57 only.
- B 49th's ITEM 1a (KS-1054) adds a third rc-1 cause (a broken python3); the wording covers it; the rebase interaction is reasoned, not run.
- shellcheck: not run.

## Collision

No local-model round on this line before (0 ladder rows name N-1350-7 other than its deploy.sh sibling brief, run today). This is ROUND 1 of 2 on the counter. No open PR touches deploy-all.sh (Premises). B 49th's ITEM 1a touches `check-startup-migrations.sh` and the ks1054 suite only.

## Scope

Closes the deploy-all.sh twin of gate47 N-1350-7 ONLY. Refs KS-1054, does NOT close it. Not in scope: deploy.sh (its own brief), N-1350-3..-6, ITEM 1a.

## Output

Exactly ONE fenced ```diff block, nothing outside it. Two sections, product first, then the new test, paths exactly as the File: and Test file: lines give them. Every `+` line on its own physical line. Every context line keeps its leading space.

files.Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/deploy-a:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# SECUURA PLATFORM — UNIFIED DEPLOYMENT SCRIPT
# =============================================================================
# Builds ALL services with a single git-hash tag and deploys them atomically
# to the target environment. Ensures all services run the same version.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy-all.sh dev              # Deploy to Azure Dev
#   ./deploy-all.sh demo             # Deploy to Azure Demo
#   ./deploy-all.sh dev --skip-build # Deploy using existing :latest images
#   ./deploy-all.sh dev --services "originate auth api-gateway"  # Subset only
#   ./deploy-all.sh dev --dry-run    # Show what would be deployed
#
# Requirements:
#   - Azure CLI logged in (az login)
#   - ACR access (secuura02demoacr)
#   - Run from repo root (Blockchain/Dev/)
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# KS-359: single source of truth for the deployment id, matching deploy.sh.
# The demo container apps are named "${DEPLOYMENT_ID}-demo-*" (e.g.
# secuura02-demo-api); deriving the prefix from here (instead of a hardcoded
# "secuura-demo") keeps deploy-all.sh in step after the secuura02 rename.
DEPLOYMENT_ID="secuura02"
ACR="${DEPLOYMENT_ID}demoacr"
ACR_URL="${ACR}.azurecr.io/secuura"

# Environment configuration (bash 3 compatible)
get_env_config() {
  local env="$1" key="$2"
  case "${env}_${key}" in
    dev_rg)     echo "secuura-dev-rg" ;;
    dev_prefix) echo "secuura-dev" ;;
    dev_domain) echo "kindtree-935b2ded.southeastasia.azurecontainerapps.io" ;;
    demo_rg)     echo "secuura-demo-rg" ;;
    demo_prefix) echo "${DEPLOYMENT_ID}-demo" ;;
    demo_domain) echo "kindtree-935b2ded.southeastasia.azurecontainerapps.io" ;;
  esac
}

# Service → Dockerfile mapping
# Format: "container-app-suffix:image-name:dockerfile-path"
BACKEND_SERVICES=(
  "api:api-gateway:services/api-gateway/Dockerfile"
  "originate:originate:services/originate/Dockerfile"
  "auth:auth:services/auth/Dockerfile"
  "anchoring:anchoring:services/anchoring/Dockerfile"
  "wallet:wallet-connector:services/wallet-connector/Dockerfile"
  "prism:prism:services/prism/Dockerfile"
  "security:security:services/security/Dockerfile"
  "analytics:analytics:services/analytics/Dockerfile"
  "timestamp:timestamping:services/timestamping/Dockerfile"
  "billing:billing:services/billing/Dockerfile"
  "tokenisation:tokenisation:services/tokenisation/Dockerfile"
  "tenant-prov:tenant-provisioning:services/tenant-provisioning/Dockerfile"
)

# Frontend services (only deployed when --include-frontend is passed)
FRONTEND_SERVICES=(
  "admin:frontend-admin:frontend/admin/Dockerfile"
  "issuer:frontend-issuer:frontend/issuer/Dockerfile"
  "verifier:frontend-verifier:frontend/verifier/Dockerfile"
)

# Optional services (only exist in some environments)
OPTIONAL_SERVICES=(
  "m365:m365-integration:services/m365-integration/Dockerfile"
  "outlook:outlook-addin:frontend/outlook-addin/Dockerfile"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parse arguments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TARGET_ENV="${1:-}"
SKIP_BUILD=false
DRY_RUN=false
INCLUDE_FRONTEND=false
SPECIFIC_SERVICES=""
SKIP_SMOKE=false

shift || true
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --skip-build) SKIP_BUILD=true ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=true ;;
    --include-frontend) INCLUDE_FRONTEND=true ;;
    --skip-smoke) SKIP_SMOKE=true ;;
    --services) SPECIFIC_SERVICES="$2"; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

if [[ -z "$TARGET_ENV" ]] || [[ "$TARGET_ENV" != "dev" && "$TARGET_ENV" != "demo" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <dev|demo> [--skip-build] [--dry-run] [--include-frontend] [--services 'svc1 svc2']"
  exit 1
fi

RG="$(get_env_config "$TARGET_ENV" rg)"
PREFIX="$(get_env_config "$TARGET_ENV" prefix)"
DOMAIN="$(get_env_config "$TARGET_ENV" domain)"
TAG="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)"

echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  SECUURA UNIFIED DEPLOYMENT                              ║"
echo "╠═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
echo "║  Environment:  ${TARGET_ENV}                                       ║"
echo "║  Resource Group: ${RG}                       ║"
echo "║  Image Tag:   ${TAG}                          ║"
echo "║  Skip Build:  ${SKIP_BUILD}                                    ║"
echo "║  Dry Run:     ${DRY_RUN}                                    ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
echo ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determine which services to deploy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY=()

if [[ -n "$SPECIFIC_SERVICES" ]]; then
  # User specified a subset
  for svc in $SPECIFIC_SERVICES; do
    for entry in "${BACKEND_SERVICES[@]}" "${FRONTEND_SERVICES[@]}" "${OPTIONAL_SERVICES[@]}"; do
      app_suffix=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f1)
      if [[ "$svc" == "$app_suffix" ]] || [[ "$svc" == "$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2)" ]]; then
        SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY+=("$entry")
      fi
    done
  done
else
  # All backend services
  SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY=("${BACKEND_SERVICES[@]}")
  # Frontend if requested
  if [[ "$INCLUDE_FRONTEND" == "true" ]]; then
    SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY+=("${FRONTEND_SERVICES[@]}")
  fi
  # Optional services only if they exist in the target environment
  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_SERVICES[@]}"; do
    app_suffix=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f1)
    app_name="${PREFIX}-${app_suffix}"
    if az containerapp show --name "$app_name" --resource-group "$RG" &>/dev/null; then
      SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY+=("$entry")
    fi
  done
fi

echo "Services to deploy (${#SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]}):"
for entry in "${SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]}"; do
  echo "  - $(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2)"
done
echo ""

if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "[DRY RUN] Would build and deploy ${#SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]} services with tag ${TAG}"
  exit 0
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build phase — parallel ACR builds
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if [[ "$SKIP_BUILD" == "false" ]]; then
  echo "═══ BUILD PHASE ═══"
  PIDS=()
  BUILD_LOGS=()

  for entry in "${SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]}"; do
    image_name=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2)
    dockerfile=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f3)

    if [[ ! -f "$dockerfile" ]]; then
      echo "  ⚠ Skipping $image_name — Dockerfile not found: $dockerfile"
      continue
    fi

    LOG="/tmp/secuura-build-${image_name}.log"
    BUILD_LOGS+=("$image_name:$LOG")

    echo "  Building $image_name..."
    az acr build --registry "$ACR" \
      --image "secuura/${image_name}:${TAG}" \
      --file "$dockerfile" . \
      > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
    PIDS+=($!)
  done

  # Wait for all builds
  FAILED=0
  for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
    if ! wait "${PIDS[$i]}"; then
      entry="${BUILD_LOGS[$i]}"
      name=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f1)
      log=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2-)
      echo "  ✗ FAILED: $name"
      tail -5 "$log"
      FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
    fi
  done

  if [[ $FAILED -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo ""
    echo "ERROR: $FAILED build(s) failed. Aborting deployment."
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "  All ${#SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]} builds succeeded."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deploy phase — update all container apps
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

echo "═══ DEPLOY PHASE ═══"
DEPLOY_FAILED=0

for entry in "${SERVICES_TO_DEPLOY[@]}"; do
  app_suffix=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f1)
  image_name=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2)
  app_name="${PREFIX}-${app_suffix}"
  image="${ACR_URL}/${image_name}:${TAG}"

  echo -n "  Deploying ${app_name}... "
  if az containerapp update --name "$app_name" --resource-group "$RG" \
    --image "$image" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "done"
  else
    echo "FAILED"
    DEPLOY_FAILED=$((DEPLOY_FAILED + 1))
  fi
done

if [[ $DEPLOY_FAILED -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo ""
  echo "WARNING: $DEPLOY_FAILED deployment(s) failed."
fi

echo ""
echo "Deployment complete. Tag: ${TAG}"
echo ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Smoke test phase
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if [[ "$SKIP_SMOKE" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "Skipping smoke tests (--skip-smoke)"
  exit 0
fi

echo "═══ SMOKE TEST PHASE (waiting 30s for containers to start) ═══"
sleep 30

API="https://${PREFIX}-api.${DOMAIN}"
PASS=0
FAIL=0
# KS-1054 / gate44 N-1346-3: a third counter. A check that did not RUN was landing in PASS and
# inflating "7 passed, 0 failed". It must not land in FAIL either — that would fail a deploy over a
# rollback to an older image whose /health has no such field.
SKIP=0

smoke_skip() { # a check that did NOT run: neither a pass nor a failure
  local name="$1"
  local why="$2"
  echo "  ⚠ $name — SKIPPED: $why (not a pass)"
  SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
}

smoke_test() {
  local name="$1"
  local expected="$2"
  local actual="$3"
  if [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]]; then
    echo "  ✓ $name"
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  else
    echo "  ✗ $name (expected $expected, got $actual)"
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  fi
}

# 1. Health
CODE=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$API/health")
smoke_test "Health check" "200" "$CODE"

# 1b. KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — startup migrations. The check above discards the BODY
# (`-o /dev/null`), so it cannot see a failed startup migration: /health answers 200 and stays
# healthy by design (Kam's option (a)), and the failure is reported in the payload. Fetch the
# body and let the shared predicate decide; it keys on `failed`, never on `error`.
HEALTH_BODY=$(curl -s --max-time 10 "$API/health")
# THREE-WAY, matching the predicate's three exit codes. `|| MIG_RC=$?` is load-bearing under
# `set -e` (:21). rc 2 is rendered as a named SKIP: it neither counts as a pass nor fails the deploy.
MIG_RC=0
"$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/check-startup-migrations.sh" "$HEALTH_BODY" || MIG_RC=$?
case "$MIG_RC" in
  0)
    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "0 failed"
    ;;
  2)
    smoke_skip "Startup migrations" "the check did not run — see above"
    ;;
  *)
    smoke_test "Startup migrations" "0 failed" "one or more failed"
    ;;
esac

# 2. Login
LOGIN_RESP=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -X POST "$API/api/auth/login" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}')
TOKEN=$(echo "$LOGIN_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('data',{}).get('accessToken',''))" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [[ -n "$TOKEN" && "$TOKEN" != "None" ]]; then
  smoke_test "Admin login" "200" "200"
else
  smoke_test "Admin login" "200" "FAIL"
fi

# 3. Platform tenants (admin only)
if [[ -n "$TOKEN" && "$TOKEN" != "None" ]]; then
  CODE=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$API/api/platform/tenants" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN")
  smoke_test "Platform tenants" "200" "$CODE"
fi

# 4. Certification
if [[ -n "$TOKEN" && "$TOKEN" != "None" ]]; then
  CERT_CODE=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "$API/api/certifications/issue" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"type":"certificate","data":{"title":"Smoke Test","issuedBy":"Deploy Script"}}')
  smoke_test "Certification issue" "201" "$CERT_CODE"
fi

# 5. Verification
VERIFY_CODE=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "$API/api/verification/verify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"contentHash":"sha256:smoketest"}')
smoke_test "Verification endpoint" "200" "$VERIFY_CODE"

# 6. RBAC — non-admin should get 403 on platform
NON_ADMIN_RESP=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -X POST "$API/api/auth/login" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"registrar@ox.ac.uk","password":"OxRegistrar123!@#"}')
NON_ADMIN_TOKEN=$(echo "$NON_ADMIN_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('data',{}).get('accessToken',''))" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [[ -n "$NON_ADMIN_TOKEN" && "$NON_ADMIN_TOKEN" != "None" ]]; then
  CODE=$(curl -s --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$API/api/platform/tenants" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $NON_ADMIN_TOKEN")
  smoke_test "RBAC: OWNER blocked from platform" "403" "$CODE"
fi

echo ""
echo "═══ SMOKE TEST RESULTS: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed, $SKIP skipped ═══"

if [[ $FAIL -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo ""
  echo "⚠ WARNING: Some smoke tests failed. Review the deployment."
  exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "✓ Deployment and smoke tests passed for ${TARGET_ENV}."
echo "  Tag: ${TAG}"
echo "  API: ${API}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — the deploy scripts read /health's startupMigrations
# =============================================================================
# The defect gate39 left open: deploy-all.sh:281 read the /health STATUS CODE only
# (`-o /dev/null` discards the body) and deploy.sh:823 grepped the body for "healthy".
# Kam's option (a) keeps /health at 200 and healthy when a startup migration FAILED, so
# neither check could ever see one: the deploy passed over a half-migrated database.
#
# The rule lives in ONE predicate, deployment/azure/check-startup-migrations.sh, so it can
# be driven directly; each deploy script is then asserted to CALL it. That split is what
# lets an arm remove the call from ONE script and red only that script's cell.
#
# KEYED ON `failed`, NEVER `error` — gate39's N-G39-2 measured a CORE statement failure
# served as `failed: N` with NO `error` field, so an `error`-keyed check reads it as clean.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1054_deploy_scripts_read_startup_migrations.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
AZ="$HERE/../../deployment/azure"
SUBJ="$AZ/check-startup-migrations.sh"
ALL="$AZ/deploy-all.sh"
ONE="$AZ/deploy.sh"

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n       %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# FIXTURE HEALTH FIRST (KS-897's lesson): if the subjects are not here, ABORT with a named
# error rather than letting every case fail and read as eleven product defects.
for f in "$ALL" "$ONE"; do
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || { echo "FATAL: subject not found at $f" >&2; exit 2; }
done

# --- the predicate, driven directly. rc is captured with NO pipeline in the measured
# --- statement: `rc=$?` after a pipe measures the LAST stage, not the subject.
probe() { # $1 label  $2 body  $3 want-rc  $4 want-substring
  if [[ ! -x "$SUBJ" ]]; then bad "$1" "predicate missing or not executable at $SUBJ"; return; fi
  local out rc
  out="$(bash "$SUBJ" "$2" 2>&1 < /dev/null)"; rc=$?
  if [[ "$rc" != "$3" ]]; then bad "$1" "rc=$rc want $3 :: $out"; return; fi
  if [[ -n "$4" && "$out" != *"$4"* ]]; then bad "$1" "output did not name '$4' :: $out"; return; fi
  ok "$1"
}

echo "=== P: the predicate ==="
probe "P1 failed 0 -> the deploy step PASSES" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":41,"failed":0}}' 0 "0 failed"
probe "P2 failed 2 -> the deploy step FAILS, although /health is 200 and healthy" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":39,"failed":2}}' 1 "2 migration(s) FAILED"
probe "P3 KEYED ON failed, NOT error: failed 3 with error null still FAILS (gate39 N-G39-2)" \
      '{"status":"healthy","error":null,"startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":0,"failed":3}}' 1 "3 migration(s) FAILED"
# 🔴 THE CONTRACT CHANGED HERE, DELIBERATELY, AND THESE THREE CELLS ARE WHY IT IS VISIBLE.
# gate44 N-1346-2/-3/-4: the predicate already distinguished THREE states in its TEXT (a clean tick,
# a named skip, a failure) and then collapsed the first two into rc 0. So neither caller could tell
# "ran clean" from "never ran", and both printed a passing line for a check that did not run.
# The fix is a THIRD EXIT CODE, rc 2 = PASS-WITH-SKIP: the deploy OUTCOME stays a pass (Kam's option
# (a), and B 43rd's rollback reasoning — an older image serves no such field and must still be
# deployable) while the printed verdict stops claiming a clean run.
# P4, P5 and P7 therefore move from rc 0 to rc 2. That is not a weakening: R1-R4 below assert that
# rc 2 still yields a PASSING deploy in BOTH callers, which is the property P4 was protecting.
probe "P4 field ABSENT (an older image) -> PASS-WITH-SKIP (rc 2), so a rollback is not blocked" \
      '{"status":"healthy"}' 2 "ABSENT"
probe "P5 a non-JSON body -> PASS-WITH-SKIP (rc 2), named, and explicitly 'not a pass'" \
      'upstream connect error' 2 "not a pass"
probe "P6 failed present but NOT an integer -> refuses to read it as zero" \
      '{"startupMigrations":{"failed":"two"}}' 1 "not an integer"
probe "P7 an EMPTY body -> PASS-WITH-SKIP (rc 2), named, never a silent pass" \
      '' 2 "not a pass"

# ---- NEW, gate44 N-1346-2: `ran:false` is the case that was genuinely different. The gateway's own
# module says ran:false "is NOT the same as a clean run", and gate44 measured it reachable three ways
# at boot (the DB late inside the KS 377 retry window, DATABASE_URL unset, or the run threw). Before
# this change it printed "0 failed" with a tick and rc 0 — the most misleading of the four shapes,
# because it names the field and reports a number. gate44's suggested shape, adopted: treat it
# exactly like ABSENT.
probe "P8 ran:false with failed 0 -> PASS-WITH-SKIP (rc 2), NOT a clean '0 failed' tick" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":false,"failed":0}}' 2 "did NOT run"
probe "P8b ran:true with failed 0 is still a CLEAN PASS (rc 0) — P8 is not an unconditional skip" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":41,"failed":0}}' 0 "0 failed"

# ---- gate44 N-1346-4, and Wednesday's ruling CHANGED my proposal here. python3 missing from PATH
# read a failed-2 body as "not JSON - SKIPPED" and rc 0: a dependency #1346 introduced that failed
# OPEN, and it also MISATTRIBUTED the cause. I proposed rc 2 (pass-with-skip, message naming the
# parser). Wednesday ruled rc 1, FAIL CLOSED, and her reasoning is the one that holds: a missing
# parser is a HOST defect, not an image property, so the rollback argument that protects the ABSENT
# case does not reach it — and deploy-all.sh ALREADY fails a deploy without python3, at its
# login-token parse, so failing closed makes deploy.sh consistent with the script beside it rather
# than inventing a new failure mode. Kam's option (a) is explicit that the deploy reads as FAILED.
echo "=== P-NOPY: python3 absent must FAIL CLOSED, and name the parser ==="
NOPY_BIN="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1054_nopy.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$NOPY_BIN"' EXIT
nopy_probe() { # $1 label  $2 body  $3 want-rc  $4 want-substring
  local out rc
  out="$(PATH="$NOPY_BIN" /bin/bash "$SUBJ" "$2" 2>&1 < /dev/null)"; rc=$?
  if [[ "$rc" != "$3" ]]; then bad "$1" "rc=$rc want $3 :: $out"; return; fi
  if [[ -n "$4" && "$out" != *"$4"* ]]; then bad "$1" "output did not name '$4' :: $out"; return; fi
  ok "$1"
}
# FIXTURE HEALTH: prove python3 really is unreachable under that PATH, or every arm below is vacuous.
if PATH="$NOPY_BIN" /bin/bash -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1'; then
  bad "P9-FIXTURE python3 is absent under the stub PATH" "python3 is still reachable — the arms below would prove nothing"
else
  ok "P9-FIXTURE python3 is absent under the stub PATH (so the arms below are not vacuous)"
fi
nopy_probe "P9 python3 absent + a failed-2 body -> FAILS CLOSED (rc 1), not read as 'not JSON'" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"failed":2}}' 1 "python3"
nopy_probe "P9b python3 absent + a CLEAN body ALSO fails closed: absence of a parser is not evidence" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"failed":0}}' 1 "python3"
# CONTROL, the same two bodies WITH python3 present, so P9/P9b are about the parser and not the body.
probe "P9c CONTROL the failed-2 body with python3 present -> rc 1 naming the migrations, not the parser" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"failed":2}}' 1 "2 migration(s) FAILED"
probe "P9d CONTROL the clean body with python3 present -> rc 0, so the stub PATH is what moved P9b" \
      '{"status":"healthy","startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":41,"failed":0}}' 0 "0 failed"
# An EMPTY body needs no parser at all, so it must still be PASS-WITH-SKIP even with python3 gone.
nopy_probe "P9e python3 absent + an EMPTY body -> still rc 2: that branch never needed a parser" \
      '' 2 "not a pass"

echo "=== C: each deploy script must CALL the predicate ==="
# Asserted per script, so an arm can remove ONE call and red only that script's cell.
if grep -q 'check-startup-migrations.sh' "$ALL"; then
  ok "C1 deploy-all.sh calls the predicate"
else
  bad "C1 deploy-all.sh calls the predicate" "no reference to check-startup-migrations.sh"
fi
if grep -q 'check-startup-migrations.sh' "$ONE"; then
  ok "C2 deploy.sh calls the predicate"
else
  bad "C2 deploy.sh calls the predicate" "no reference to check-startup-migrations.sh"
fi

# C3 is the reason 1b exists at all: the ORIGINAL check discards the body, so it can never
# see a failed migration. If someone "simplifies" deploy-all.sh back to the status code alone,
# this reds.
if grep -q 'HEALTH_BODY=$(curl' "$ALL"; then
  ok "C3 deploy-all.sh fetches the /health BODY, not only the status code"
else
  bad "C3 deploy-all.sh fetches the /health BODY" "no body fetch; -o /dev/null discards it"
fi

# C4: /health itself must NOT be made to fail. Kam's option (a) is explicit that the service
# keeps serving; a deploy-side check that also flipped /health would contradict the ruling.
if grep -q 'stays 200' "$SUBJ" 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "C4 the predicate records that /health stays 200 and the DEPLOY is what fails"
else
  bad "C4 the predicate records that /health stays 200" "the ruling's shape is not stated in the subject"
fi

echo "=== E: deploy.sh must EXIT NON-ZERO, not merely log (gate44 N-1346-1) ==="
# The defect: verify_deployment counted ERRORS and its last command was `log_error`, an echo, so it
# returned 0 and the deploy read as successful over failed startup migrations. deploy-all.sh already
# exits 1 on a failed smoke test; deploy.sh did not.
#
# HOW THIS IS DRIVEN, and why not a grep. A grep for `return 1` passes on a COMMENTED-OUT line, and
# a line-number pin drifts. So the REAL summary block is extracted from deploy.sh by its own marker
# and EXECUTED, with the log_* helpers stubbed and ERRORS injected. What runs is the product's bytes.
SUMMARY_MARKER='# ── Summary ─'
SUMMARY_HITS=$(grep -c "$SUMMARY_MARKER" "$ONE" || true)
if [[ "$SUMMARY_HITS" != "1" ]]; then
  bad "E0 the summary block is locatable by marker" "expected 1 occurrence of the marker in deploy.sh, found $SUMMARY_HITS"
else
  ok "E0 the summary block is locatable by marker (1 occurrence, so the extraction is unambiguous)"
fi

# Strip the function's closing brace; keep everything else byte-for-byte.
SUMMARY_BLOCK=$(awk -v m="$SUMMARY_MARKER" 'index($0,m){f=1} f&&/^}/{exit} f{print}' "$ONE")

# 🔴 gate46 N-1348-6, fixed below at E1 and mitigated here. The driver stubbed ONLY log_success and
# log_error, so an edit that dropped the `return` and ended the branch on an UNSTUBBED helper exited
# 127 — non-zero — and E1's `!= "0"` test passed while the real deploy.sh exited 0 over failed
# migrations. Two changes close it: every log_* helper the script uses is stubbed here, and E1 now
# requires rc EXACTLY 1 rather than merely non-zero.
_summary_prelude() { # $1 ERRORS  $2 SKIPS
  printf 'log_success() { printf "SUCCESS %%s\n" "$*"; }\n'
  printf 'log_error() { printf "ERROR %%s\n" "$*"; }\n'
  printf 'log_warn() { printf "WARN %%s\n" "$*"; }\n'
  printf 'log_info() { printf "INFO %%s\n" "$*"; }\n'
  printf 'ERRORS=%s\nSKIPS=%s\n' "$1" "$2"
}
drive_summary_io() { # $1 ERRORS  $2 SKIPS -> runs the real block, stdout is its output, rc is its rc
  local errors="$1" skips="$2"
  {
    _summary_prelude "$errors" "$skips"
    printf '__ks1054_verify() {\n'
    printf '%s\n' "$SUMMARY_BLOCK"
    printf '}\n__ks1054_verify\n'
  } > "$TMPDRV"
  bash "$TMPDRV" 2>&1 < /dev/null
}
drive_summary_out() { drive_summary_io "$1" "$2"; }           # its printed lines
drive_summary_rc()  { drive_summary_io "$1" "$2" > /dev/null 2>&1; printf '%s' "$?"; }
drive_summary() { # $1 ERRORS value -> prints the rc of the real block (SKIPS pinned at 0)
  local errors="$1" rc
  {
    _summary_prelude "$errors" 0
    # 🔴 gate45 N-1348-2, and it is the finding that mattered. The block was executed at TOP LEVEL,
    # where `return N` is ITSELF AN ERROR for every N (rc 1 on bash 3.2, rc 2 on bash 5). So this cell
    # measured the rc of a malformed `return`, never the return VALUE — with the product changed to
    # `return 0` the suite still read 14/0 while the real deploy.sh exits 0 over failed migrations.
    # The red proof could not fail. Wrapping the block in a function makes the RETURN VALUE the rc,
    # which is the property E1 claims to pin. A return 1 -> return 0 tamper of deploy.sh reds E1
    # (driven by hand at round 2 and by gate46; not automated in this file).
    # 🔴 gate46 N-1348-7: this comment used to say "The TAMPER_RETURN_ZERO arm below drives it."
    # `git grep -n TAMPER_RETURN_ZERO` found that line and nothing else — there was no such arm, so
    # the file made a false statement about itself and that statement landed on develop. Corrected
    # here rather than in #1348, because a new head would have voided the gate that graded it.
    printf '__ks1054_verify() {\n'
    printf '%s\n' "$SUMMARY_BLOCK"
    printf '}\n__ks1054_verify\n'
  } > "$TMPDRV"
  bash "$TMPDRV" > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null; rc=$?
  printf '%s' "$rc"
}
# 🔴 gate45 N-1348-1: `mktemp -t ks1054_summary_drive` carries NO X's. GNU coreutils REFUSES that,
# so TMPDRV was empty and `bash ""` exited 127 — E2 red, and E1 green for the wrong reason. CI's
# ubuntu-latest runs this suite (pr-security-gates.yml -> run-shell-suites.sh) and develop's copy is
# 11/0 there, so the no-X form was a NEW RED of this seat's making. A template with X's is portable.
TMPDRV="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1054_summary_drive.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$TMPDRV"' EXIT

if [[ -z "$SUMMARY_BLOCK" ]]; then
  bad "E1 deploy.sh's verify summary FAILS the deploy when it counted issues" "the summary block extracted EMPTY — the marker moved; this is a fixture failure, not a product result"
  bad "E2 CONTROL: the same block PASSES when it counted none" "the summary block extracted EMPTY"
else
  RC_FAIL=$(drive_summary 2)
  # 🔴 gate46 N-1348-6: this test was `!= "0"`, which accepts ANY non-zero rc — including the 127 an
  # unstubbed helper produces. Under that hole an edit that dropped the `return` kept the suite green
  # while the real script exited 0 over failed migrations. EXACTLY 1 is the property being pinned.
  if [[ "$RC_FAIL" == "1" ]]; then
    ok "E1 deploy.sh's verify summary exits non-zero when it counted issues (rc=$RC_FAIL)"
  else
    bad "E1 deploy.sh's verify summary exits non-zero when it counted issues" "rc=0 with ERRORS=2 — it logged the failure and returned success, so the deploy reads as OK"
  fi
  # E2 is the arm that stops E1 passing for the wrong reason: if the block exited non-zero
  # unconditionally, a clean verification would also fail the deploy, which is worse.
  RC_OK=$(drive_summary 0)
  if [[ "$RC_OK" == "0" ]]; then
    ok "E2 CONTROL: the same block exits 0 when it counted none, so E1 is not an unconditional failure"
  else
    bad "E2 CONTROL: the same block exits 0 when it counted none" "rc=$RC_OK with ERRORS=0 — a clean verification would fail the deploy"
  fi
fi

echo "=== R: the CALLERS must render the third state — a SKIP is neither a pass nor a failure ==="
# WHY THESE CELLS EXIST, and the moment that proved it. With the predicate returning rc 2 and the
# callers untouched, this suite read 22 passed / 0 failed — while deploy.sh would have FAILED a
# deploy over an ABSENT startupMigrations field, because `if ! predicate` reads rc 2 as a failure.
# That is the rollback regression B 43rd's P4 exists to prevent, and no P-cell could see it: the
# P-cells drive the predicate, and this is a property of the CALL SITES. So each caller's own bytes
# are extracted and executed below, with a STUB predicate that exits with a chosen rc.

# ---- deploy.sh's startup-migration CALL SITE, its own bytes, against a stub predicate ----
CALL_MARKER='# KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — startup migrations. A grep for "healthy"'
CALL_HITS=$(grep -cF "$CALL_MARKER" "$ONE" || true)
if [[ "$CALL_HITS" != "1" ]]; then
  bad "R0 deploy.sh's migration call site is locatable by marker" "expected 1 occurrence, found $CALL_HITS"
else
  ok "R0 deploy.sh's migration call site is locatable by marker (1 occurrence, extraction unambiguous)"
fi
# Everything from the marker to the `esac` that closes the three-way case, byte-for-byte.
# 🔴 THE TERMINATOR IS `esac` AND MY FIRST VERSION USED `fi`. Before this change the block ended in a
# `fi`; the three-way case ends in `esac`, so the old pattern ran past the block to the `fi` closing
# the enclosing `if [ -n "$API_FQDN" ]` at :880 and swallowed the login check as well. All three
# call-site cells went red on a product that was correct. The INSTRUMENT moved, not the subject.
CALL_BLOCK=$(awk -v m="$CALL_MARKER" 'index($0,m){f=1} f{print} f&&/^        esac$/{exit}' "$ONE")

drive_callsite() { # $1 = the rc the stub predicate exits with -> prints "ERRORS=<n> SKIPS=<n>"
  local stubrc="$1" dir
  dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1054_callsite.XXXXXX")"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit %s\n' "$stubrc" > "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
  chmod +x "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
  {
    printf 'log_error() { printf "ERROR %%s\\n" "$*"; }\n'
    printf 'log_warn() { printf "WARN %%s\\n" "$*"; }\n'
    printf 'log_info() { printf "INFO %%s\\n" "$*"; }\n'
    printf 'log_success() { printf "SUCCESS %%s\\n" "$*"; }\n'
    printf 'ERRORS=0\nSKIPS=0\nAPI_HEALTH=\x27{"status":"healthy"}\x27\n'
    # WRAPPED IN A FUNCTION, and that is required rather than tidy: the block declares
    # `local MIG_RC=0`, and `local` outside a function is an error in bash. Same reason the E-cells
    # wrap the summary block. What runs is still the product's own bytes.
    printf '__ks1054_callsite() {\n'
    printf '%s\n' "$CALL_BLOCK"
    printf '}\n__ks1054_callsite\n'
    printf 'printf "ERRORS=%%s SKIPS=%%s\\n" "$ERRORS" "${SKIPS-unset}"\n'
  } > "$dir/drive.sh"
  ( cd "$dir" && bash ./drive.sh 2>/dev/null < /dev/null | tail -1 )
  rm -rf "$dir"
}

if [[ -z "$CALL_BLOCK" ]]; then
  bad "R1 rc 2 from the predicate is a SKIP, not an ERROR" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
  bad "R2 rc 1 from the predicate is still an ERROR" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
  bad "R3 rc 0 from the predicate is neither" "the call-site block extracted EMPTY"
else
  R_SKIP=$(drive_callsite 2)
  # THE ROLLBACK RULE, and it is the whole point of the third state: rc 2 must NOT count an ERROR.
  if [[ "$R_SKIP" == "ERRORS=0 SKIPS=1" ]]; then
    ok "R1 rc 2 counts a SKIP and NOT an error, so an ABSENT field still yields a passing deploy"
  else
    bad "R1 rc 2 counts a SKIP and NOT an error" "got '$R_SKIP', want 'ERRORS=0 SKIPS=1' — rc 2 read as a failure would block a ROLLBACK"
  fi
  R_FAIL=$(drive_callsite 1)
  if [[ "$R_FAIL" == "ERRORS=1 SKIPS=0" ]]; then
    ok "R2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts an ERROR, so the third state did not weaken the real check"
  else
    bad "R2 CONTROL rc 1 still counts an ERROR" "got '$R_FAIL', want 'ERRORS=1 SKIPS=0'"
  fi
  R_CLEAN=$(drive_callsite 0)
  if [[ "$R_CLEAN" == "ERRORS=0 SKIPS=0" ]]; then
    ok "R3 CONTROL rc 0 counts neither, so R1 is not an unconditional skip"
  else
    bad "R3 CONTROL rc 0 counts neither" "got '$R_CLEAN', want 'ERRORS=0 SKIPS=0'"
  fi
fi

# ---- deploy.sh's SUMMARY must render PASS-WITH-SKIP without claiming a clean run ----
if [[ -n "$SUMMARY_BLOCK" ]]; then
  S_OUT=$(drive_summary_out 0 1)
  S_RC=$(drive_summary_rc 0 1)
  if [[ "$S_RC" == "0" ]]; then
    ok "R4 ERRORS=0 with SKIPS=1 still PASSES the deploy step (rc 0) — the rollback rule holds"
  else
    bad "R4 ERRORS=0 with SKIPS=1 still PASSES the deploy step" "rc=$S_RC — a skipped check must not fail the deploy"
  fi
  if [[ "$S_OUT" != *"all checks OK"* ]]; then
    ok "R5 ...and it does NOT print 'all checks OK', so it stops claiming a clean run"
  else
    bad "R5 it must NOT print 'all checks OK' when a check was SKIPPED" "printed: $S_OUT"
  fi
  if [[ "$S_OUT" == *"SKIP"* ]]; then
    ok "R6 ...and it NAMES the skip, so a check that stopped checking is not silent"
  else
    bad "R6 it must NAME the skip" "printed: $S_OUT"
  fi
  S_CLEAN_OUT=$(drive_summary_out 0 0)
  if [[ "$S_CLEAN_OUT" == *"all checks OK"* ]]; then
    ok "R7 CONTROL with SKIPS=0 it still prints 'all checks OK', so R5 is not an unconditional gag"
  else
    bad "R7 CONTROL SKIPS=0 must still print 'all checks OK'" "printed: $S_CLEAN_OUT"
  fi
fi

# ---- deploy-all.sh must count a SKIP separately and must not fail the deploy for it ----
# 🔴 R8 USED TO BE `grep -q smoke_skip`, AND A TAMPER CAUGHT IT. Replacing the skip CALL with a
# `smoke_test ... "0 failed" "0 failed"` — the exact regression this cell exists to stop, which puts
# a check that did not run back into the PASS count — left the `smoke_skip()` DEFINITION in the file,
# so the grep still matched and the suite stayed GREEN. A presence-grep cannot see whether the path
# is wired. So deploy-all.sh's own call site is now extracted and EXECUTED, like deploy.sh's.
ALL_MARKER='# 1b. KS-1054 / N-1332-5 — startup migrations.'
ALL_HITS=$(grep -cF "$ALL_MARKER" "$ALL" || true)
if [[ "$ALL_HITS" != "1" ]]; then
  bad "R8a deploy-all.sh's call site is locatable by marker" "expected 1 occurrence, found $ALL_HITS"
else
  ok "R8a deploy-all.sh's call site is locatable by marker (1 occurrence, extraction unambiguous)"
fi
ALL_BLOCK=$(awk -v m="$ALL_MARKER" 'index($0,m){f=1} f{print} f&&/^esac$/{exit}' "$ALL")

drive_all_callsite() { # $1 = stub predicate rc -> prints "PASS=<n> FAIL=<n> SKIP=<n>"
  local stubrc="$1" dir
  dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1054_allsite.XXXXXX")"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit %s\n' "$stubrc" > "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
  chmod +x "$dir/check-startup-migrations.sh"
  {
    # The REAL counter semantics, copied from deploy-all.sh's own helpers: a pass increments PASS,
    # a mismatch increments FAIL, a skip increments SKIP. Stubbing them is what lets the block's
    # OWN dispatch decide which one moves.
    printf 'PASS=0; FAIL=0; SKIP=0\n'
    printf 'smoke_test() { if [ "$3" = "$2" ]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); fi; }\n'
    printf 'smoke_skip() { SKIP=$((SKIP+1)); }\n'
    printf 'API=http://127.0.0.1:1\nHEALTH_BODY=\x27{"status":"healthy"}\x27\n'
    printf 'curl() { printf %%s "$HEALTH_BODY"; }\n'
    printf '%s\n' "$ALL_BLOCK"
    printf 'printf "PASS=%%s FAIL=%%s SKIP=%%s\\n" "$PASS" "$FAIL" "$SKIP"\n'
  } > "$dir/drive.sh"
  ( cd "$dir" && bash ./drive.sh 2>/dev/null < /dev/null | tail -1 )
  rm -rf "$dir"
}

if [[ -z "$ALL_BLOCK" ]]; then
  bad "R8 rc 2 increments SKIP and neither PASS nor FAIL" "the deploy-all call-site block extracted EMPTY"
else
  A_SKIP=$(drive_all_callsite 2)
  if [[ "$A_SKIP" == "PASS=0 FAIL=0 SKIP=1" ]]; then
    ok "R8 rc 2 increments SKIP and NEITHER PASS nor FAIL, so it is not counted as a passing check"
  else
    bad "R8 rc 2 increments SKIP and neither PASS nor FAIL" "got '$A_SKIP', want 'PASS=0 FAIL=0 SKIP=1'"
  fi
  A_PASS=$(drive_all_callsite 0)
  if [[ "$A_PASS" == "PASS=1 FAIL=0 SKIP=0" ]]; then
    ok "R8b CONTROL rc 0 still increments PASS, so R8 is not an unconditional skip"
  else
    bad "R8b CONTROL rc 0 still increments PASS" "got '$A_PASS', want 'PASS=1 FAIL=0 SKIP=0'"
  fi
  A_FAIL=$(drive_all_callsite 1)
  if [[ "$A_FAIL" == "PASS=0 FAIL=1 SKIP=0" ]]; then
    ok "R8c CONTROL rc 1 still increments FAIL, so the third state did not weaken the real check"
  else
    bad "R8c CONTROL rc 1 still increments FAIL" "got '$A_FAIL', want 'PASS=0 FAIL=1 SKIP=0'"
  fi
fi
# R9 is STRUCTURAL and is labelled as such: it reads the results LINE, which prints no counter this
# harness can drive without running the whole smoke phase against a live stack.
if grep -q 'SMOKE TEST RESULTS: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed, $SKIP skipped' "$ALL"; then
  ok "R9 (structural) the SMOKE TEST RESULTS line reports the skip count beside pass and fail"
else
  bad "R9 (structural) the results line reports the skip count" "the results line does not carry \$SKIP"
fi
# The exit rule must stay keyed on FAIL alone, or a SKIP would fail the deploy.
if grep -qE '^\s*if \[\[ \$FAIL -gt 0 \]\]; then' "$ALL"; then
  ok "R10 deploy-all.sh still exits non-zero on FAIL alone, so a SKIP never fails the deploy"
else
  bad "R10 deploy-all.sh exits on FAIL alone" "the exit condition changed shape; a SKIP may now fail the deploy"
fi

echo
echo "ks1054 deploy startupMigrations: $pass passed, $fail failed"
[[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
